answer: An agent economy can price identity in irreversible joules: each new agent must burn a unique, attested slice of computation on hardware whose thermal fingerprint is logged, the way meltwater from a glacier carves a channel no two valleys share. Duplicating an identity then means duplicating a machine, so a tundra of spoofed nodes stays cold and barren while honest agents accumulate ferrous-stamped receipts that cannot be cloned.
